name: Finding the unusual and the break
gist: Spotting when a time series behaves abnormally or suddenly changes character. This includes detecting anomalies, change points, and out-of-distribution events in sequences.
explain: Every sequence has a baseline—the normal range of behavior. A healthy patient's blood pressure stays in a narrow band. A factory bearing vibrates at expected frequencies. Stock prices move within historical ranges. But sometimes something changes. A patient's blood pressure spikes. A bearing starts vibrating at a new frequency, signaling wear. A stock crashes on bad news. These events matter enormously for action: hospitals need to alert staff, factories need to schedule maintenance, traders need to reduce risk. The challenge is that 'unusual' is not always obvious. Is today's temperature 2 degrees warmer than average because the model is wrong, or because climate is shifting? Is a sensor reading an anomaly or just normal noise? Is a change temporary or permanent?

The problem has layers. Anomalies can be sudden spikes, slow drifts, or behavioral changes that are subtle. A sequence can have multiple normal modes—for example, traffic patterns differ on weekdays and weekends, and both are normal. Anomalies can be local, affecting just a small window, or global, shifting the entire distribution. Some anomalies are contextual: an absence of data in a hospital system is normal during maintenance but would be alarming in production. And rare events are, by definition, rare, so labeled training data is scarce. The model has to learn what normal looks like from mostly-normal data, then spot when something deviates.

Papers tackle this by learning baseline models of normal sequences, then flagging values that deviate far from the baseline. Some use reconstruction error: if an autoencoder encodes and decodes the sequence, large reconstruction error suggests anomaly. Others explicitly model change points—moments when the distribution shifts—and estimate where they occur. Some combine statistical tests with neural methods. A key insight is that anomalies are often domain-specific: in healthcare, you care about medical significance, not just statistical significance, so papers sometimes incorporate domain knowledge or causal reasoning to separate true anomalies from noise.

papers.title: Adaptive Conformal Anomaly Detection with Time Series Foundation Models for Signal Monitoring.
papers.contribution: Achieves strong performance combining simplicity, interpretability, robustness, and adaptivity while maintaining out-of-sample guarantees without model fine-tuning.

papers.title: Contextual and Seasonal LSTMs for Time Series Anomaly Detection
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets, demonstrating effectiveness for robust time series anomaly detection.

papers.title: Enhancing Sparse Event Detection in Healthcare Time-Series via Adaptive Gate of Context–Detail Interaction
papers.contribution: The framework achieves substantial performance gains over DETR-based models across arrhythmia, emotion, and activity detection, with particularly strong improvements on sparse events.

papers.title: ICDiffAD: Implicit Conditioning Diffusion Model for Time Series Anomaly Detection
papers.contribution: Improves F1 score by 20.2% and reduces false positives by 60.23% compared to existing diffusion-based TSAD methods.

papers.title: Low Rank Transformer for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection and Localization
papers.contribution: ALoRa-T and ALoRa-Loc significantly outperform state-of-the-art methods in both anomaly detection and localization tasks on multivariate time series.

papers.title: PaAno: Patch-Based Representation Learning for Time-Series Anomaly Detection
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on TSB-AD benchmark for univariate and multivariate anomaly detection, significantly outperforming methods based on heavy architectures.

papers.title: When Foundation Models are One-Liners: Limitations and Future Directions for Time Series Anomaly Detection
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that anomaly detection performance of foundation models does not significantly differ from simple baselines, revealing fundamental limitations in reconstruction and forecasting-based methodologies.

papers.title: When to Retrain after Drift: A Data-Only Test of Post-Drift Data Size Sufficiency
papers.contribution: CALIPER consistently matches or exceeds the best fixed data size for retraining across heterogeneous datasets, learner families, and detectors while incurring negligible overhead.

papers.title: AnomSeer: Reinforcing Multimodal LLMs to Reason for Time-Series Anomaly Detection
papers.contribution: Outperforms larger commercial baselines on classification and localization; produces plausible reasoning traces supporting conclusions.

papers.title: Beyond Euclidean Summaries: Online Change Point Detection for Distribution-Valued Data
papers.contribution: Detects complex distributional shifts with reduced detection delay at matched ARL0 compared with moments-based and model-free baselines through sequential detectors on tangent fields.

papers.title: Beyond Markovian Drifts: Action-Biased Geometric Walks with Memory for Personalized Summarization
papers.contribution: Outperforms specialized personalized summarizers by 0.41 PerSEval and strong LLM baselines by 0.22 with cross-domain robustness of 0.19 over best LLM.

papers.title: COGNOS: Universal Enhancement for Time Series Anomaly Detection via Constrained Gaussian-Noise Optimization and Smoothing
papers.contribution: COGNOS consistently enhances performance of state-of-the-art backbones across multiple benchmarks through statistical regularization coupled with adaptive filtering.

papers.title: Causal Feature Learning via Generalized Rayleigh Quotients
papers.contribution: Achieves 93.69% average fault detection rate on Tennessee Eastman Process, outperforming 15 baseline methods and validating benefit of jointly capturing temporal relevance and environment mean invariance.

papers.title: Change Point Localization and Inference in Dynamic Multilayer Networks
papers.contribution: First consistency results for change point localization in dynamic network data with limiting distributions under vanishing/non-vanishing jump regimes and data-driven confidence intervals.

papers.title: Cluster-Aware Causal Mixer for Online Anomaly Detection in Multivariate Time Series
papers.contribution: Consistently achieves superior performance across six public benchmarks for online multivariate time-series anomaly detection.

papers.title: Complexity- and Statistics-Guided Anomaly Detection in Time Series Foundation Models
papers.contribution: We identify two key challenges when applying TFMs to reconstruction-based anomaly detection and propose solutions.

papers.title: EVEREST: A Transformer for Probabilistic Rare-Event Anomaly Detection with Evidential and Tail-Aware Uncertainty
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art True Skill Statistic scores of 0.973, 0.970, and 0.966 at 24, 48, and 72-hour horizons for C-class flares with 0.81M parameters.

papers.title: Free Point-wise Anomaly Detection via Fold-bifurcation
papers.contribution: FOLD is parameter-free, requires no anomaly labels, and achieves competitive or superior performance on 40 benchmarks against 34 baselines with particular strength under strict point-wise evaluation.

papers.title: Hierarchical ODE: Learning Continuous-Time Physical Prototypes for Early Link Failure Detection
papers.contribution: The method extracts underlying physical prototypes for robust failure detection on early link failure detection tasks with irregularly sampled time series.

papers.title: IMPACT: Influence Modeling for Open-Set Time Series Anomaly Detection
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art on open-set time series anomaly detection across varying settings and contamination rates.

papers.title: MPFM: Cross Multi-Domain Prototype Flow Matching for Log Anomaly Detection
papers.contribution: Delivers substantial gains on HDFS, BGL, Thunderbird, and Spirit datasets under multi-domain joint training.

papers.title: Online Change Point Detection for Multivariate Inhomogeneous Poisson Processes Time Series
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical guarantees on false alarm probability and characterization of detection delay; develops new Matrix Bernstein inequality for temporally dependent processes.

papers.title: PGRF-Net: A Prototype-Guided Relational Fusion Network for Diagnostic Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive detection performance on five benchmarks while providing interpretable decomposition of anomaly scores into four distinct evidence sources.

papers.title: PYRREGULAR: A Unified Framework for Irregular Time Series, with Classification Benchmarks
papers.contribution: The repository centralizes irregular time series research and enables robust evaluation of temporal data analysis methods across diverse domains.

papers.title: QuITE: Query-Based Irregular Time Series Embedding
papers.contribution: Up to 54.7% average relative gains in forecasting and 15.8% in classification; works as plug-and-play module for diverse backbones.

papers.title: TeamWork: Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection via Asymmetric Role-aware Channel Modeling
papers.contribution: Achieves superior performance compared with state-of-the-art methods on real-world multivariate time series anomaly detection datasets.

papers.title: Towards Foundation Models for Zero-Shot Time Series Anomaly Detection: Leveraging Synthetic Data and Relative Context Discrepancy
papers.contribution: TimeRCD outperforms existing foundation models in most zero-shot TSAD settings while remaining competitive with dataset-specific baselines.

papers.title: Towards Multimodal Time Series Anomaly Detection with Semantic Alignment and Condensed Interaction
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive or superior results on six real-world multimodal datasets through semantic alignment and condensed interaction.
